title: Projection identities and Frobenius factorization for arbitrary finite-field models
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $q=p^a$, $a\geq1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and $k$ is its fixed algebraic closure. Let $T_0$ be any $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base], with no finite-type or separatedness hypothesis. Put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-pc-base-change], with projections $\pi:T\to T_0$ and $\rho:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $F_0=F_{T_0}^{(q)}$ and $F=F_T^{(q)}$ be the absolute $q$-power Frobenii [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. The morphism $F_0$ is over $k_0$; hence its base change $\Phi=F_0\times\operatorname{id}_k$ is defined. Put $\sigma(z)=z^q$, $\gamma=\sigma^{-1}$ as in [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], and $g_\epsilon=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\epsilon)$ for $\epsilon=\sigma,\gamma$, using the spectrum functor [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then
$$
 \pi F=F_0\pi,\quad \rho F=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\rho,\quad
 \pi\Phi=F_0\pi,\quad \rho\Phi=\rho,\quad
 \pi g_\sigma=\pi,\quad \rho g_\sigma=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\rho,
$$
and the following equalities hold as scheme morphisms:
$$
 F=g_\sigma\Phi=\Phi g_\sigma,\qquad
 \Phi=g_\gamma F=Fg_\gamma,\qquad
 g_\sigma g_\gamma=g_\gamma g_\sigma=\operatorname{id}_T.
$$
Here composition is written right to left. For any morphism $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ of arbitrary $k_0$-schemes and its base change $f:X\to Y$, the corresponding endomorphisms satisfy $f\Phi_X=\Phi_Yf$ and $fF_X^{(q)}=F_Y^{(q)}f$.

proof.text: Use model_characteristic and model_frobenius_over from def-weil-relative-frobenius-geometric-fiber for arbitrary schemes over the finite base. These already prove characteristic inheritance and descent of q-power model Frobenius, including the empty scheme.

Use the proved source-library lemma Scheme.comp_iterateFrobenius (AbsoluteFrobeniusNatural) for naturality of the recorded absolute Frobenius. This lemma proves equality on underlying spaces and on every section by preservation of powers under ring homomorphisms; it has only global p-vanishing hypotheses and so covers empty schemes.

Identify q-power Frobenius on Spec k with Spec of arithmetic Frobenius using ext_to_Spec and GammaSpecIso_inv_naturality: both global ring maps send x to x^(p^a), since Nat.card k0=q=p^a and coe_frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic is the cardinality-power map. Apply the preceding naturality lemma to the two pullback projections. The remaining four projection identities are Over.pullback_map_left, the over-morphism equation, and galoisMap_projections.

For each order of the composite of base-changed model Frobenius and arithmetic coefficient Frobenius, compare its two projections with absolute Frobenius using the six projection equations. pullback.hom_ext gives both arithmetic factorizations.

The already proved galoisMap_inverse gives both inverse composites of arithmetic and geometric coefficient Frobenius. Substitute each arithmetic factorization and use associativity with the corresponding inverse identity to obtain the two geometric cancellation equalities.

Apply Scheme.comp_iterateFrobenius to the underlying model morphism. Over-morphism extensionality upgrades the equality to the slice category, and functoriality of Over.pullback transports it to the scalar extensions; taking the left component proves model-Frobenius naturality. Apply Scheme.comp_iterateFrobenius directly to the scalar-extended morphism for absolute-Frobenius naturality.
